students.name: Aanal Kumar
students.bio: Aanal Kumar is an animator and visual storyteller from Kolkata with over 14 years of experience in motion and design. He is driven by the belief that motion is powerful because it makes things feel alive; in a static world, movement is what connects people to reality. His professional journey is highlighted by his independent short film, The Hook , which won a "Best Animation" Jury Award and was showcased on the El-Rey Network in Los Angeles. Over the years, Aanal has worked across a variety of environments, from creative production houses to his recent role as a Senior Specialist at Protiviti. It was there that he realized design is more than just a "facelift"—it is a vital tool for solving problems and telling stories clearly. A "player" at heart, Aanal is an avid trekker who loves exploring the mountains. He believes that seeing the world from different perspectives makes him a better designer. He also studied theater at Rangkarmee, which helped him develop a disciplined approach to being a team player. Aanal often says that if animation is the body, design is the soul. He is now at CIID to bring these two worlds together, using his 14 years of expertise to move toward human-centric design that creates a real impact on people's lives.

students.name: Anke Westphal
students.bio: Hi, I'm Anke (or Nika as most people refer to me as). I have a Master's degree in Communication Design from HTWG Konstanz - University of Applied Sciences. This master's helped to deepen my conceptual and research-driven process, allowing me to better understand the complexity that surrounds us so I can create better, more robust solutions for the future. My work is driven by the question of purpose in design. Rather than only shaping surfaces, I aim to make things more accessible, meaningful, and socially responsible. Ethical and social perspectives strongly guide my work, even though navigating real-world constraints can be challenging. I enjoy analytical thinking and developing concept-driven solutions tailored to people's actual needs. Working across disciplines excites me, and I value the insights that emerge where design meets other fields. My Master's thesis explored prisoner resocialization — an unexpected but deeply human context for design. Born in the North, raised in the East, and living in the South of Germany for many years, I feel most comfortable in the in-between — between perspectives, environments, and ideas. I'm excited to continue this journey at CIID and to learn alongside people from diverse backgrounds.

students.name: Hannah Dusch
students.bio: Hannah is a communication design student from Germany. My main areas of experience are visual communication and graphic design. During my Bachelor's degree, I also studied product design, which broadened my understanding of design processes and thinking across disciplines. In my design practice, I love combining analogue and digital methods and experimenting with different techniques. I'm really excited to explore new tools and approaches at CIID, and to learn in an international, interdisciplinary environment. One topic I'm very passionate about is intersectional feminism, particularly how design can be used as a tool for reflection, participation and social change. I would like to research this further during my time at CIID. Outside of design, I'm an active person who enjoys being outdoors and doing sports. I also love getting creative in my free time, reading, and learning new languages. I studied in Italy for my entire Bachelor's degree and I'm very excited to return!

students.name: Julian Mößnang
students.bio: Julian Mößnang is a graphic designer from Munich, Germany, where he also completed his Bachelor's degree. During his studies in Brand and Communication Design, he focused on classical graphic design while exploring ways to challenge established rules, pushing the boundaries and uncovering the potential of visual communication. During his Bachelor's thesis, he examined how sensory stimulation can support relaxation. His project involved a spatial installation engaging four senses — hearing, sight, touch, and smell. The autonomous installation was designed for airport environments, has been proven effective, and offers travelers a space to relax while on the move. For his Master's degree, Julian moved to Constance in southern Germany. There, he began a Master's in Communication Design at HTWG Konstanz, focusing on new interpretations of design, spatial installations, experimenting with different tools, and integrating multiple media within single projects. Together with fellow students, he also took over the KD—Lounge project, which is well known in the field of graphic design at HTWG.

students.name: Pauline Kuhrdt
students.bio: I'm a communication designer working at the intersection of research, system thinking, and emerging technologies. My practice is less about styling and more a tool for me to understand structures and translate them into formats that make complexity accessible. I work conceptually and process-driven. Research, conversations, and iterative prototyping are central to how I like to work. Many of my projects combine physical and digital elements, moving between editorial design, visual systems, and interactive prototypes. I'm especially interested in how code and computational tools can expand my design practice. At CIID, I want to move my communication design background further into the field of interaction design. I'm aiming to strengthen my computational skills, work hands-on with new technologies, and develop a more technical understanding of how digital systems behave. A field that particularly interests me is the connection between nature and computation and how natural processes, patterns, and behaviors can inform interactive systems, and how technology can help us sense, translate, or reinterpret natural phenomena in meaningful ways.

students.name: Roshni Prajapati
students.bio: Roshni Prajapati is a design practitioner from India who enjoys working at the intersection of design, technology, and creativity. With a background in engineering, she brings an analytical lens to her work while staying deeply curious about how people think and behave. Her practice spans product, interaction, accessibility, and motion design, with a growing interest in AI and immersive technologies. Outside structured design work, Roshni enjoys creating art, exploring new tools, and sharing small experiments and explorations with the Figma Community. When she needs to reset, Roshni turns to trekking, hiking, and the mountains, where slowing down and observing nature helps her return with fresh perspective and clarity - often grounding her in one of her core principles: living life with no regrets.

students.name: Sarah Lu
students.bio: Originally from France, Sarah has been based in London for the past decade, where she has worked in innovation, service design, and user research across leading design consultancies. Her work spans both the public and private sectors, with clients including the NHS, Jaguar Land Rover, Girlguiding, and the Bank of Scotland. She is particularly drawn to projects with strong social value, where craft, curiosity, and multidisciplinary thinking are central to the work. Sarah is especially interested in the potential of design to support ageing populations and explore new models of co‑living, and she hopes to contribute to work in this space in the future. As her practice has evolved into design leadership, she focuses on creating team environments where people feel supported, encouraged to challenge one another, and able to grow professionally. Outside of work, Sarah enjoys adrenaline in small doses. She surfskates and coaches surfskating in her spare time and, as a beginner surfer, has recently added snowboarding to her growing list of board sports.

students.name: Shaheen Shrestha
students.bio: Shaheen is a product designer from Nepal, currently based in Paris. She grew up in a household filled with artists and entrepreneurs. She found joy in doodling, drawing, and painting. In school, she studied psychology & business which awakened her interest in cognitive behaviours and how businesses run which today is crucial for creating user centric products. Currently her work focuses on turning early-stage chaos into clear, shippable products. She thrives under pressure and aligns scattered teams to ship results fast. She is driven to create products that positively impact society by leveraging data, design, and behavioral psychology. Apart from work she dabbles in photography, cooks nourishing meals, works out to stay fit and travels to new places.

students.name: Taylor Haigler
students.bio: Taylor is a user experience designer from Brooklyn, NY with a background in art history and archaeology and experience in design and technology consulting. She's interested in how thoughtful design can make complex systems—particularly in healthcare and public services—more human, accessible, and easier to navigate. Her interests are increasingly drawn toward interaction design and how digital and physical experiences intersect. She enjoys experimenting with new tools exploring how well-designed interactions can make everyday services more intuitive and supportive. Outside of design, Taylor practices yoga, studies Spanish, and loves being near the water. She's naturally curious about people and places and interested in how design can support wellbeing and care in everyday life.

students.name: Thea Arndt
students.bio: I'm from Germany and I'm currently studying for a Master's degree in Communication Design. So far in my studies, I have mainly focused on visual communication and information design. I also gained experience in interaction design during my semester abroad. I'm particularly interested in how design can facilitate new ways of thinking that go beyond products. In my current favourite book, How to Do Nothing, Jenny Odell describes how important it is to create space for deeper, creative impulses and authentic encounters in an increasingly fast-paced and consumer-oriented society. During my time at CIID, I would therefore like to explore ways of taking a fresh look at what already exists and drawing more attention to nature and local communities. I am particularly looking forward to interdisciplinary exchange, combining different techniques and ideas, learning about new approaches and collaborating to find innovative solutions. Outside of work, I enjoy spending time outdoors, practising creative writing, and exploring topics related to the environment, nutrition, and society – preferably through reading books.

students.name: Varun Thandassery Ramakrishnan
students.bio: Varun is an engineer by degree and transitioned into product design after choosing to pursue his long standing interest in design. Since then, he has worked on building digital products across marketing and financial technology, with a focus on translating complex systems into intuitive user experiences. Motivated to broaden his creative and technical perspective, Varun is joining Copenhagen Institute of Interaction Design (CIID) to explore new ways of shaping meaningful interactions between technology and human behaviour. Outside of work, Varun enjoys playing football, travelling, and gaming.

students.name: Yisi Liu
students.bio: Yisi is an artist, designer, and landscape architect with a decade of practice at the intersection of ecology, design and built environment. Her work spans a range of scales and geographies, from a rehabilitation park designed for people with disabilities in the heart of a city, to the first boarding school for girls in Afghanistan, to a master plan revitalizing an abandoned airport into a new sustainable community. Her research has investigated the ecological impact of fracking across the United States and explored how vacant land can become an economic catalyst for underserved communities in Boston. In recent years, Yisi has shifted her focus toward the digital frontier, exploring how technology can deepen the relationship between people and the physical environment. Her projects include transforming intangible data from the nature into interactive art, deploying AR and VR to help communities imagine and co-create their future public spaces, and creating virtual environments that guide communities to build their own gardens When she's not "reshaping" the landscape, Yisi is a dedicated collage artist, modern art enthusiast, and nature lover who finds equal inspiration in a gallery and on a trail. She draws energy from moving between creative identities.
